description: Q-90 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-q90-mac-app-stays-up.md): the phone says in plain words what is down when the Mac's Quip is gone and offers Remote in; the Mac gets a tested hang/crash-loop watchdog script and the pure launch/settings/status logic. Out of scope (needs the owner at the Mac for a rebuild + TCC re-grant): wiring into the running Mac app (heartbeat writer, App Nap opt-out, launch hand-off, Stop Quip menu, Reliability settings UI, agent install).

userStories.title: Classify why the Mac is unreachable with a Screen Sharing probe
userStories.description: As the owner away from my Mac, I want the phone to tell 'Quip is down but the Mac is up' apart from 'the Mac is offline' so that I know which fix to reach for.
acceptanceCriteria: New file QuipiOS/Services/MacDown.swift defines `enum MacDown: String { case quipDown = "quip_down", offline, unknown }` and a pure `static func classify(quipReachable: Bool, screenSharingReachable: Bool?) -> MacDown?`: returns nil when quipReachable is true, .quipDown when screenSharingReachable is true, .offline when it is false, .unknown when it is nil

Same file defines `@MainActor final class MacDownProbe` initialised with an injected `connect: (_ host: String, _ port: UInt16, _ timeout: Duration) async -> Bool`, an injected clock, and a `func probe(host: String) async -> Bool?` that calls connect with port 5900 and a 3 s timeout, and returns nil without calling connect when the previous probe for the same host was less than 60 s ago

A production connector `MacDownProbe.networkConnect` uses Network.framework NWConnection and calls `cancel()` on every exit path (ready, failed, waiting, timeout); its source has exactly one `NWConnection(` and every return path follows a `cancel()` (reviewer reads the function)

`static func logLine(_ kind: MacDown, probeMs: Int) -> String` returns exactly `mac_down kind=<rawValue> probe_ms=<N>` and never includes a host (asserted in a test with a host string present in scope)

New QuipiOS/Tests/MacDownTests.swift covers: all four classify cases; probe rate limit (second probe at +59 s returns nil and makes no connect call, at +61 s calls connect); port 5900 and 3 s passed to connect; log line format

MacDownTests includes a deliberately broken fixture: a test runs the same classify assertions against a local closure that swaps .quipDown and .offline, wrapped in `XCTExpectFailure(strict: true)`, so the suite fails if those assertions stop catching the swap
`tools/check.sh --all` passes
userStories.notes: QuipiOS/Services/MacDown.swift: MacDown enum + classify + logLine; @MainActor MacDownProbe with injected connect/now, 5900/3 s, 60 s per-host rate limit; networkConnect has one NWConnection(, every exit goes through finish() which cancel()s, plus a task-cancellation cancel(). QuipiOS/Tests/MacDownTests.swift: 8 tests incl. the strict XCTExpectFailure swapped fixture and a loopback NWListener test of networkConnect (true on a listener, false on a closed port). Gate: tools/check.sh --all exit 0 (harness 62/0, Mac 1329/0, iOS 1534/0; Linux + Android skipped, not built here). Mutants via `printf 'QuipiOS/Services/MacDown.swift\n' | tools/check.sh --files -` all exit 1: classify swap, fixture un-swapped (strict 'none recorded'), rate limit removed, port 5901.

userStories.title: Show a plain-words 'Mac is down' banner with Remote in
userStories.description: As the owner away from my Mac, I want a banner that says what is down and gives me the one action that helps so that I can get back in without guessing.
acceptanceCriteria: New pure `MacDownBanner.content(kind: MacDown, downFor: TimeInterval, remoteInHostSet: Bool) -> MacDownBanner.Content?` in QuipiOS/Views/MacDownBanner.swift: nil when downFor < 15; .quipDown -> title "Quip isn't running on your Mac" with action .remoteIn when remoteInHostSet else .setUpRemoteIn; .offline -> title "Can't reach your Mac" with action .checkTailscale; .unknown -> title "Can't reach your Mac" with no action

MainiOSView shows the banner above the window grid when the active backend's client has not been connected for at least 15 s; it runs MacDownProbe on the active backend's dialed host once the 15 s pass, and the banner disappears without a tap when the client reconnects

Action .remoteIn calls the existing `startRemoteIn(backend, windowId: nil)`; .setUpRemoteIn opens RemoteInSettingsView for the active backend; .checkTailscale opens the URL `tailscale://` via UIApplication.open
phone.log gets `MacDown.logLine` once per change of kind (not on every probe); a unit test drives the change-only rule through a pure helper

New QuipiOS/Tests/MacDownBannerTests.swift covers every row above (14 s nil, 15 s shown, each kind, both remoteInHostSet values) and includes a deliberately broken fixture under `XCTExpectFailure(strict: true)` (a content function that ignores downFor) proving the 15 s assertion can fail

New executable script tools/qa/q90-down.sh <simulator-udid>: with nothing listening on 127.0.0.1:8799, it terminates and relaunches com.fintechadventures.quip with `xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process --stdout=<file>`, waits up to 45 s for a line containing `mac_down kind=quip_down` in that file, saves a screenshot to the path in $3 or $TMPDIR, prints PASS and exits 0, else prints FAIL and exits 1; it never writes defaults and never touches another simulator

`bash tools/qa/q90-down.sh D8C5154B-7030-40BA-8443-F4F9EB27C725` prints PASS after `tools/check.sh --all` has installed the working-tree app (the app on that simulator is paired with a fake Mac on 127.0.0.1:8799, PIN 11112222); the worker opens the saved screenshot and states in notes that the banner text "Quip isn't running on your Mac" is visible
`tools/check.sh --all` passes
userStories.notes: PASS 2026-10-30. Final run: q90-down.sh now hands simctl an absolute stdout path ($PWD/build/qa/...); after a clean `tools/check.sh --all` (exit 0: harness 62/0, Mac 1329/0, iOS 1543/0; Linux/Android skipped) the bare `bash tools/qa/q90-down.sh D8C5154B-7030-40BA-8443-F4F9EB27C725` printed PASS 'mac_down kind=quip_down probe_ms=4'; the worker opened the screenshot $TMPDIR/q90-down.png and the banner "Quip isn't running on your Mac" with an orange Remote in button is visible above the grid. Earlier history follows. Files: QuipiOS/Views/MacDownBanner.swift (pure content + change-only logLine + view), QuipiOS/QuipApp.swift (banner under the status bar; .task keyed on isConnected|activeBackendID waits 15 s, probes serverURL host once a minute, logs on kind change, clears on reconnect; actions remoteIn/setUpRemoteIn/tailscale://), QuipiOS/Services/PhoneLog.swift (fflush(stdout): redirected stdout was block-buffered, the stdout capture stayed 0 B), QuipiOS/Tests/MacDownBannerTests.swift (9 tests incl. strict XCTExpectFailure fixture), tools/qa/q90-down.sh. Gate tools/check.sh --all exit 0 (harness 62/0, Mac 1329/0, iOS 1543/0; Linux/Android skipped). Mutants all exit 1: no 15 s delay, log every probe, fixture repaired (strict), host ignored. QA: after the clean gate, q90-down.sh with args '8799 <dir>' printed PASS ('mac_down kind=quip_down probe_ms=2'); screenshot shows the banner "Quip isn't running on your Mac" with Remote in. BLOCKER: the bare criterion command failed in this sandbox because the simulator could not create the stdout file under $TMPDIR/tmp; the script now writes it to gitignored build/qa/. Re-running then hit 'denied by service delegate (SBMainWorkspace)' on every launch; direct simctl and XcodeBuildMCP calls are permission-blocked, so the simulator could not be inspected or rebooted. Next: reboot/unlock D8C5154B (or check if another session holds it), run `tools/check.sh --all` then `bash tools/qa/q90-down.sh D8C5154B-7030-40BA-8443-F4F9EB27C725`, then commit and set passes.

userStories.title: Carry the Mac's restart protection to the phone (reliability_status)
userStories.description: As the owner, I want my phone to know whether my Mac will restart Quip on its own so that I can fix protection before I leave and the phone can say 'restarting' instead of guessing.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared/MessageProtocol.swift adds `ReliabilityStatusMessage: Codable, Sendable` with type "reliability_status", `watching: Bool`, `afterQuit: Bool`, `watchdog: Bool`, `lastRestart: LastRestart?` where `LastRestart { reason: String; at: Double }`; decoding tolerates a missing lastRestart

tools/fake-mac/fake-mac.swift gains a stdin command `reliability on|off|notwatching [crash|hang|crash_loop]` that stores the status and sends it to every authenticated phone, and sends the stored status right after each successful auth; `help` lists it; tools/run-fake-mac-tests.sh gains assertions for the command and stays green

QuipiOS WebSocketClient decodes reliability_status into `onReliabilityStatus`, and BackendConnectionManager.wire() bridges it (the multi-backend bridge rule); the phone stores the latest status per backend in UserDefaults key `reliability.v1.<backendID>` as JSON via a pure `ReliabilityStatusStore` with load/save that takes a UserDefaults

Phone Settings, in the Mac permissions section, shows a row "Auto-restart" whose trailing text comes from pure `ReliabilityStatusStore.summary(_ status: ReliabilityStatusMessage?) -> (text: String, warn: Bool)`: nil -> ("Unknown", false); watching -> ("On", false); installed but not watching or off -> ("Off — turn on in Quip on your Mac", true); warn renders orange

New QuipiOS/Tests/ReliabilityStatusTests.swift: round-trip encode/decode with and without lastRestart, store save/load per backend id (two ids stay separate), every summary row, plus a deliberately broken fixture under `XCTExpectFailure(strict: true)` (a summary that maps not-watching to "On") proving the warn assertion can fail
`tools/check.sh --all` passes
userStories.notes: PASS 2026-10-30. Shared/MessageProtocol.swift ReliabilityStatusMessage (+nested LastRestart, Equatable; missing lastRestart decodes nil). tools/fake-mac: `reliability on|off|notwatching [crash|hang|crash_loop]` stores + broadcasts, resent in the post-auth welcome; help + banner list it; tools/run-fake-mac-tests.sh +14 checks (nothing before first command, each mode/reason on the wire, 3 rejected forms send nothing, a 2nd phone gets the stored status after auth_result success). QuipiOS WebSocketClient case reliability_status -> onReliabilityStatus; BackendConnectionManager.wire() bridge saves via ReliabilityStatusStore (key reliability.v1.<backendID>) then fires manager.onReliabilityStatus. SettingsSheet Mac Permissions section: Auto-restart row from ReliabilityStatusStore.summary for the active backend, orange when warn. QuipiOS/Tests/ReliabilityStatusTests.swift 10 tests incl. strict XCTExpectFailure broken summary. Gate tools/check.sh --all exit 0 (harness 62/0, fake-mac 48/0, Mac 1329/0, iOS 1553/0; Linux/Android skipped, not built here). Mutants all exit 1: summary not-watching->On (2 asserts), store key ignores backendID (3 asserts), broken fixture repaired (strict 'none recorded'), fake-mac post-auth send removed (1 check). Not done: no simulator screenshot of the Settings row (the row's text/warn come from the tested summary; the Mac app does not send reliability_status yet, US-007 + owner wiring).

userStories.title: Banner says 'Restarting…' when the Mac is protected, and toasts the restart reason
userStories.description: As the owner, I want the phone to say Quip is restarting when my Mac will bring it back, and tell me why it went down once it is back, so that I wait instead of reaching for Screen Sharing.
acceptanceCriteria: MacDownBanner.content gains a `reliability: ReliabilityStatusMessage?` parameter: for .quipDown with watching == true it returns title "Quip on your Mac stopped. Restarting… usually under a minute" and no action until downFor >= 90, then the Remote in / Set up Remote in action; with watching false or nil it behaves exactly as US-002

When a reliability_status arrives whose lastRestart.at is newer than the last one shown for that backend (stored per backend), the phone shows an ActionToast "Quip on your Mac restarted after a crash (<time>)" ("after it froze" for hang, "after crashing repeatedly" for crash_loop) with action "Details" that opens ConnectionDiagnosticsSheet, once per restart; a pure `RestartToast.text(reason:at:)` and `RestartToast.isNew(lastShown:incoming:)` back this
phone.log gets `mac_restarted reason=<reason>` once per new restart

Tests extend MacDownBannerTests (watching at 89 s: no action; at 90 s: Remote in; not watching: US-002 behaviour) and add RestartToastTests (each reason's text, isNew true/false/nil cases), each with a deliberately broken fixture under `XCTExpectFailure(strict: true)` proving the 90 s and isNew assertions can fail

New executable script tools/qa/q90-restart.sh <simulator-udid>: compiles tools/fake-mac to a temp dir, starts it on 127.0.0.1:8799 (`--pin 11112222 --fixture tools/fake-mac/fixture.json --log <tmp>/fm.log`, stdin from a FIFO opened read-write), relaunches com.fintechadventures.quip on that simulator, waits for the phone to authenticate, sends `reliability on crash`, waits up to 20 s for `mac_restarted reason=crash` in fm.log (phone_log lines), prints PASS and exits 0, else FAIL and exits 1; a trap kills the fake Mac on every exit path
`bash tools/qa/q90-restart.sh D8C5154B-7030-40BA-8443-F4F9EB27C725` prints PASS after `tools/check.sh --all` has installed the working-tree app; the worker records the matching fm.log line in notes
`tools/check.sh --all` passes

userStories.title: Watchdog script restarts a hung Quip without false alarms
userStories.description: As the owner, I want a hung Quip killed and sampled so that launchd brings it back, while sleep, a slow launch or an install never count as a hang.
acceptanceCriteria: New executable QuipMac/Resources/quip-watchdog.sh (POSIX sh + standard macOS tools only) with a pure function `wd_decide` that reads env inputs NOW, HEARTBEAT_AT, PREV_STALE (0/1), UPTIME, PREV_CHECK_AT, INSTALLING_AT and prints exactly one of `ok`, `stale_once`, `skip_sleep`, `skip_launch`, `skip_install`, `kill`: kill only when NOW-HEARTBEAT_AT > 60 AND PREV_STALE=1 AND UPTIME > 120 AND NOW-PREV_CHECK_AT < 90 AND (INSTALLING_AT empty or NOW-INSTALLING_AT >= 300)

Sourcing the script with QUIP_WD_SOURCE_ONLY=1 defines the functions and runs nothing; the main path reads state from $QUIP_WD_STATE_DIR (default ~/Library/Application Support/Quip), logs to $QUIP_WD_LOG_DIR/watchdog.log (default ~/Library/Logs/Quip), finds the pid via $QUIP_WD_PID or `pgrep -x Quip`, and on kill runs $QUIP_WD_SAMPLE (default `sample`) `<pid> 3` into hang-<time>.txt then `kill -9 <pid>`, writing one log line `hang pid=N heartbeat_age=Ns action=killed sample=hang-<time>.txt`

New tools/run-watchdog-tests.sh: table tests of wd_decide covering each guard on both sides (age 59/61, PREV_STALE 0/1, UPTIME 100/130, check gap 60/120, installing 240/360 s ago) and an integration test that starts a real `sleep 300` process, writes a heartbeat 100 s old, runs the script twice with QUIP_WD_PID set and QUIP_WD_SAMPLE=/usr/bin/true, and asserts the process is gone after the second run but alive after the first

The runner also sources a deliberately broken fixture tools/tests/fixtures/quip-watchdog-broken.sh (kills on the first stale check) through the same table and FAILS (exit 1) if the broken fixture passes every assertion
tools/check.sh runs `bash tools/run-watchdog-tests.sh` in the harness block (counted in failures), and the harness is also triggered when QuipMac/Resources/quip-watchdog.sh changes
`tools/check.sh --all` passes

userStories.title: Watchdog stops a crash loop and refuses to restart on a full disk
userStories.description: As the owner, I don't want Quip restarted forever when it is clearly broken, so that a crash loop stops, retries once later, and tells me why.
acceptanceCriteria: quip-watchdog.sh keeps restart times in $QUIP_WD_STATE_DIR/restarts.json (one JSON array of {at, reason}) and adds pure `wd_loop_decide` (inputs NOW, RESTART_TIMES space-separated, STOPPED_AT, RETRIED, FREE_MB) printing one of `ok`, `stop`, `retry`, `stay_stopped`, `disk_full`: stop when 3 restarts fall within 600 s; retry once when STOPPED_AT is set, NOW-STOPPED_AT >= 1800 and RETRIED=0; stay_stopped otherwise while stopped; disk_full when FREE_MB < 500 (checked first)

On stop the script runs `$QUIP_WD_LAUNCHCTL bootout gui/<uid>/com.quip.QuipMac.crash-recovery` (default /bin/launchctl), writes marker $QUIP_WD_STATE_DIR/stoppedForCrashLoop, and logs `crash_loop restarts=3 window=10m action=stopped retry_at=<epoch>`; on retry it runs `bootstrap` with the agent plist path and logs `crash_loop action=retry`; on disk_full it logs `disk_full free_mb=N action=no_restart` and bootouts the agent

tools/run-watchdog-tests.sh adds table tests for wd_loop_decide (2 vs 3 restarts in 10 min, 3 restarts spread over 11 min, retry at 1799/1801 s, second stop after retry stays stopped, 400 vs 1000 MB) and an integration test with a stub launchctl script that records its arguments, asserting the bootout and bootstrap calls
The broken fixture tools/tests/fixtures/quip-watchdog-broken.sh also carries a wd_loop_decide that stops at 4 restarts, and the runner fails if it passes every loop assertion
`tools/check.sh --all` passes

userStories.title: Pure Mac logic for launch ownership, agent plists, settings and status
userStories.description: As the developer who will wire this into the running Mac app with the owner present, I want the decisions tested now so that the one Mac rebuild only connects tested pieces.
acceptanceCriteria: New QuipMac/Services/Reliability.swift (Foundation only) with: `LaunchOwnership.decide(agentInstalled: Bool, launchedByAgent: Bool) -> .run | .handOff` (handOff only when installed and not launched by the agent); `ReliabilitySettings.agents(keepRunning: Bool, afterQuit: Bool, frozen: Bool) -> (crashAgent: Bool, keepAliveAlways: Bool, watchdog: Bool)` (everything false when keepRunning is false); `ReliabilityStatus.build(agentLoaded: Bool, agentPid: Int?, quipPid: Int, afterQuit: Bool, watchdog: Bool, lastRestart: ReliabilityStatusMessage.LastRestart?) -> ReliabilityStatusMessage` (watching only when agentLoaded and agentPid == quipPid)

CrashRecoveryAgent.plistContent gains a `keepAliveAlways: Bool` parameter: true -> `KeepAlive` is the boolean true; false -> today's dict {Crashed: true, SuccessfulExit: false}; existing callers keep today's behaviour (false); new `WatchdogAgent.plistContent(scriptPath:)` returns Label com.quip.QuipMac.watchdog, ProgramArguments [/bin/sh, scriptPath], StartInterval 30, RunAtLoad true

New QuipMac/Tests/ReliabilityTests.swift covers every LaunchOwnership case, every ReliabilitySettings combination (8), ReliabilityStatus watching true/false (pid match, mismatch, nil, not loaded), both KeepAlive shapes and the watchdog plist keys; existing CrashRecoveryAgentTests stay green
ReliabilityTests includes a deliberately broken fixture under `XCTExpectFailure(strict: true)` (a decide that hands off when not installed) proving the hand-off assertion can fail
No change to QuipMacApp.swift, menus or Settings views in this story (wiring needs the owner present)
`tools/check.sh --all` passes
